run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:04:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans on the proxy's own ingress operation: ~0.0103 error spans/s against ~10.35 ingress spans/s at 13:20Z, and the alert's own value (0.0111) is of the same small magnitude. The proxy's errors come from its upstream calls, not from its own process: Envoy-format access logs show (a) a 12:45Z cluster of 504 'UT response_timeout' on /api/data where the frontend took 19.7-22.0s and exceeded the proxy's 15s response timeout, with the ad service's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds at 19.70s and its flagd ResolveBoolean call returning gRPC code 4 next to a flagd span with 'context deadline exceeded'; (b) a sustained trickle of 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' where the frontend upstream closed the connection before sending any response (roughly one every 1-2 minutes from 12:45:51Z through 13:14:24Z, and the sampled 503 traces contain no frontend span at all); and (c) a ~12-second burst of frontend-generated HTTP 500s on /api/cart and /api/checkout (13:07:41Z-13:07:53Z) that began 19s after the single-replica cart Deployment was rolled out at 13:07:19Z-13:07:22Z and ended when the new cart pod came up. The frontend pod itself never restarted, produced no error-status spans and its memory was flat (228->249 MiB), but it runs with a 100m CPU limit and is CFS-throttled in 33-43% of periods throughout the window, which is a plausible aggravator of the connection terminations rather than a proven cause. Because the alert fires on error rate > 0, the small but persistent 503 UC trickle alone is sufficient to keep it firing; the 504 and 500 clusters add to it. Two unrelated in-window failures were also found (cart rollout, fraud-detection OOMKill) and are reported separately; the frontend-proxy symptom is explained at the level of 'frontend upstream terminates connections / is too slow', but the exact frontend-side mechanism could not be verified because the frontend container produced no readable log lines and Jaeger holds no traces after ~12:52Z.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emits real error spans on its ingress operation: at 13:20Z the service's ingress spans ran at 10.347/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET and 0.01033/s STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and its 'router frontend egress' client spans at 10.354/s UNSET and 0/s ERROR (client spans record error=true as a tag instead of ERROR status).

frontend-proxy ingress error rate by span name over the window: 0.1724/s at 12:46:49Z falling to ~0.111/s through 12:50:49Z, then 0.0074-0.0222/s from 12:51:49Z to 13:07:49Z, a burst of 0.3519-0.3630/s at 13:08:49Z-13:12:49Z, and 0.0037-0.0185/s from 13:13:49Z to 13:22:49Z; the 'router frontend egress' error series mirrors only the 13:08-13:12 burst (0.344/s).

frontend-proxy access logs show Envoy '504 UT response_timeout' on GET /api/data and /api/data?contextKeys=... at 12:45:08Z-12:45:26Z, each with a 15000-15002 ms duration, i.e. the proxy's 15s response timeout fired against the frontend.

The same logs show repeated '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with 95 bytes sent, upstream cluster 'frontend', at 12:45:51Z, 12:46:47Z, 12:47:03Z, 12:48:19Z, 12:50:23Z, 12:51:26Z, 12:52:39Z, 12:53:53Z, 12:55:44Z and 12:55:56Z on /api/products/*, /api/recommendations and /api/cart, and again at 13:08:36Z-13:08:37Z, 13:09:42Z, 13:11:55Z and 13:14:24Z.

In the sampled error traces from frontend-proxy (12:45:18Z-12:52:40Z, 55 spans, 0 omitted), the 503 ingress spans have status_tags {error=true, http.status_code=503} and their child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true" with http.status_code="0", while the same traces contain no frontend-service span for that request; the one 504 trace (trace d4af8b1eed12c220415e404f05a06a0a) shows the proxy ingress at 15.00s/504 while the frontend GET /api/data ran 21.970s and returned 200.

In that 504 trace the frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds took 19.700281s, the ad service's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds took 19.700281s, the ad-side flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans took 2.801012s and 5.498914s with rpc.grpc.status_code="4" (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), and the flagd server span carried otel.status_description="context deadline exceeded" with rpc.grpc.status_code="2".

Between 13:07:41Z and 13:07:52Z the proxy logged ~39 HTTP 500 responses, all 'via_upstream' with 21-byte bodies and 1-3 ms durations, exclusively for /api/cart (GET and POST) and /api/checkout (POST); the frontend, not the proxy, generated those 500s. No 5xx other than a few 503 UC appears in the 13:12:00Z-13:14:24Z log range.

The 500 burst coincides with a cart Deployment rollout: Events show 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1' at 13:07:19Z, creation of pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz at 13:07:19Z, SuccessfulDelete of pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and 'Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0' at 13:07:22Z; ReplicaSets list cart-84889c965d as cart revision 2 created 13:07:19Z with the same image reference ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, i.e. a configuration-only change with one replica.

The replacement cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz was CPU-throttled in 90.0% of CFS periods at 13:09:49Z (0.4545 at 13:14:49Z, 0.1983 at 13:19:49Z) versus 0.226-0.339 for the old cart pod, while the frontend pod ran at a CFS throttle ratio of 0.33-0.43 in every sample from 12:47Z to 13:21Z and frontend-proxy at 0.07-0.12.

frontend and frontend-proxy run with very small CPU limits (frontend limit cpu 100m / memory 200Mi, request 50m/100Mi; frontend-proxy limit cpu 30m, request 15m), and the frontend pod's memory working set was flat (228.0 MiB at 12:46Z rising slowly to 248.8 MiB at 13:22Z) with restart count 0, so no OOM or restart is involved on frontend.

Frontend latency degraded only mildly and transiently: the fraction of frontend spans >5s was 0.0187 at 12:47:01Z, fell to 0 by 12:52Z, showed 0.0008 only at 13:09:49Z-13:13:49Z and 0 afterwards, and outside those minutes frontend produced no error-status spans at all (all frontend operation error rates returned 0, e.g. GET, GET /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.*, executing api route).

Traffic was not the trigger: frontend-proxy ingress span rate rose from 4.91/s at 12:47:01Z to ~12.4/s by 12:53Z and stayed at 12.26-12.97/s through 13:19:49Z, dropping only at the very end of the window (7.54/s at 13:21:49Z, 2.78/s at 13:23:49Z); the error episodes at 12:46Z and 13:08Z-13:12Z do not coincide with traffic increases.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready with 0 restarts at query time except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh, whose container lastState is terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-16T13:12:49Z (restartCount 1); all five nodes report Ready with no pressure conditions.

The cart service itself recorded no error spans in the window (POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 3.00/s, AddItem 1.64/s, EmptyCart 0.55/s, HGET 4.64/s, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET; its only ERROR series is flagd EventStream at 0), and /api/cart requests through the proxy were returning 200 at 13:05:21Z-13:05:24Z, so the 13:07Z cart-related 500s are consistent with cart having no serving endpoint after its pod was deleted, not with cart returning application errors.

The flagd ConfigMap flagd-config currently sets flag cartFailure to state ENABLED with defaultVariant "on" while other fault flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, etc.) default to "off" or 0; this is the flagd file content as served at query time, not the evaluated state during the window.

flagd flag-evaluation errors are chronic background noise across several services rather than confined to the proxy error episodes: EventStream/ResolveBoolean error rates of 0.0037-0.0051/s appear intermittently for ad, fraud-detection and recommendation across 12:47Z-13:23Z.

By 13:10Z-13:20Z the ad service had recovered: all oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans were <=1000ms (le="1000.0" equals le="+Inf" at 0.8367/s; le="100.0" 0.7953/s), so the 19.7s ad latency is a past episode, not the current state.

The sustained component that keeps RequestErrorRate above 0 is the frontend upstream terminating connections before any response (503 UC), not the proxy itself: Envoy's response detail names the frontend cluster as the upstream, the frontend pods were Ready with zero restarts, and no frontend span exists for those requests. The exact frontend-side mechanism (aborted keep-alive connection, event-loop starvation or per-request abort) cannot be pinned down because the frontend container yielded no readable log lines.

The frontend's 100m CPU limit and its steady 33-43% CFS throttling are a plausible aggravator of the frontend connection terminations and slow responses, but the throttling ratio is flat across the window and does not spike at 12:46Z or 13:08Z, so throttling alone does not explain the timing of the error episodes.

The ad service's flagd-evaluation stalls (ResolveBoolean reaching gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED with 'context deadline exceeded', 19.70s GetAds) drove the 12:45Z proxy 504 cluster, since the proxy's own 15s response timeout fired while the frontend was waiting on that ad call; the later 503 UC trickle is not explained by ad latency because ad was fast again by 13:10Z.

The cart Deployment's configuration-only rollout at 13:07:19Z-13:07:22Z removed the service's only replica and produced the 13:07:41Z-13:07:53Z frontend 500 burst on /api/cart and /api/checkout, which contributes to the 13:08:49Z-13:12:49Z proxy error-rate burst; this is a change-induced cause distinct from the 503 UC trickle.

The cartFailure fault flag (currently defaultVariant "on" in flagd-config) is not supported as the cause of the cart-path 500s: /api/cart returned 200 through the proxy at 13:05:21Z-13:05:24Z, the cart service recorded no error spans in the window, and the 500s are confined to the ~12s during which the cart pod was being replaced.

The fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 13:12:49Z, restart 1) has no observed tie to the frontend-proxy errors: the proxy's later 503 UC hits (13:14:24Z) are on /api/products, the 500 burst on /api/checkout ended at 13:07:53Z roughly five minutes before the OOM, and no checkout error or fraud-detection error span was observed after 13:12Z. It remains a separate failure on that pod with unverified consequences.

The frontend service itself is not reporting application errors: every frontend error series in traces_span_metrics_calls_total is 0 for its operations, so frontend's own instrumented work is not failing even though the proxy fails upstream calls to it; the slow-span evidence (1.9% >5s at 12:47Z) is limited to the ad-driven episode.

Capture frontend container stdout/stderr (it returned zero readable log lines for the whole window) and enable proxy retries/upstream keepalive tuning so that a 503 upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on an idempotent GET is retried instead of surfacing as a user-visible error; correlate Envoy upstream connection source ports with frontend keep-alive timeouts to confirm the reuse race.

Raise or remove the frontend's 100m CPU limit (33-43% CFS throttling is chronic) and give cart more than one replica or a PodDisruption/surge setting so a config-only rollout does not take the sole endpoint out of service and turn into frontend 500s.

gaps: No alerting rule named RequestErrorRate exists in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data), so the alert's exact expression, metric, lookback and 'for' duration could not be verified; the 1.1% value in the alert annotation could not be reproduced from a single metric.

The frontend container produced zero readable log lines for 12:43Z-12:50Z and 13:00Z-13:26Z, so there is no application-side evidence of why the frontend terminated upstream connections (503 UC) or returned 500s.

Jaeger holds no traces for frontend-proxy after ~12:52:40Z (traces_search for 13:08Z-13:13Z returned no_data), so the 13:07Z-13:12Z error burst could only be studied from access logs and metrics, not from spans.

The exact frontend/proxy keep-alive and idle-timeout settings could not be inspected: the frontend-proxy configuration is not in any otel-demo ConfigMap (only flagd-config, otel-collector, product-catalog-products, kube-root-ca.crt exist), so the connection-reuse-race hypothesis remains untested.
change_history is not integrated, so what actually changed in the cart Deployment (revision 1 -> 2, same image tag) and in flagd (revision 2 at 12:38:04Z) at those times is unknown.

The runtime flag evaluation state during the window is unknown; only the current flagd-config content (cartFailure default "on") is visible, and the flagd/flagd-ui containers produced no readable log lines.
Impact of the fraud-detection OOMKill and 1 restart at 13:12:49Z on checkout/payment paths was not verified.

No comparable long baseline exists: the cluster's pods and metric series only start at ~12:36Z-12:47Z (source_start_at values), so an hour-scale baseline for frontend-proxy error rate, ad latency and throttle ratios is unavailable.
next_steps: Inspect the frontend-proxy (Envoy) bootstrap/route configuration and the frontend Node keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout for a mismatch that produces upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, and add a retry policy for idempotent GETs.
Review the change_history or deployment audit trail for the cart Deployment revision 2 (13:07:19Z) and the flagd Deployment revision 2 (12:38:04Z) to identify what was changed and by whom.

Collect frontend application logs from the node (or enable them) around 12:45Z and 13:07Z-13:14Z to identify whether the frontend aborted connections, hit a crash-guard, or failed its gRPC dependencies.
Confirm whether the alert is expected to treat a >0 threshold as meaningful; if a small steady 503 rate is tolerable, set a non-zero threshold rather than paging on any error.
Check the fraud-detection memory limit versus usage (limit 400Mi, request 200Mi) to explain the OOMKill at 13:12:49Z and decide whether it needs remediation.
